name: K.A.R. 28-16-27: emergency or accidental discharge of sewage; report to the department
operator: Kansas Department of Health and Environment (regulation)
status_reason: Immediate report to KDHE; planned bypass needs 7 days' notice and approval; no public notice.
notes: Quote: "Emergency or accidental discharge of sewage or other materials detrimental to the quality of waters of the state shall be immediately reported to the state department of health by the owner of the treatment plant or his representative." KDHE forms and Kansas Rural Water guidance state 24 hours and a 5-day written report.

name: City of Leavenworth Sanitary Sewer Overflow Transparency Reports and per-event SSO pages
waters_covered: Missouri River tributaries in Leavenworth (Three Mile Creek, Five Mile Creek and storm drains)
access_detail: WebFetch read the index (years 2020 to 2026, newest first); curl gets 403 'Access Denied'. Per-event pages titled e.g. 'Sanitary Sewer Overflow in the 1200 block of Metropolitan reported Thursday Oct. 23, 2025'. Semiannual EPA reports also posted (2018 example).
cadence: per event, posted by the city
status_reason: The only dated per-event SSO notices found in Kansas; small city, scrape needs a browser-like client.

name: City of Topeka stream advisories (Utilities, topeka.org news)

status_reason: Dated authority advisories naming the stretch to avoid; but a 2025 Oakland plant overflow got no public notice ('no threat to the public', KDHE said no advisory needed).
